lots.working: Keep: the series is a commodity line, so I use the lower quartile of recent same-title sales ($35) rather than the $15 floor: 35 / 1.198 = 29.2, round down to $25 (all-in $29.95). Flip: likely resale is the Gowans median $50 hammer (no other sold evidence); less about 15% vendor commission = $42.50; postage n/a (pickup slab); 42.50 / 2.396 = 17.7, round down to $15. Flipping is not worthwhile. Inbound freight $0 (local pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah).
lots.confidence_reason: Hundreds of opened same-title Gowans sales, but species is only the catalogue's word (no label or mark to read) and size and thickness are unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Tasmanian Special Timbers $9,200 / $12,000 (page opened, no price on it; the $12,000 slab is the BTTO giant birdseye, 4.4 m, not comparable). Macrocarpa pine series dropped as a different timber (kept only as a downside note: median about $20 if the species is wrong). Researcher's '8 zero-price lots since June' corrected to 2 in March 2026. Gumtree kept only as a snippet lead.
lots.key_photo_findings: Chalk 1121 and 16/10/26 with lot sticker. Wider slab with waney live edge both sides, rough bandsaw marks, pale golden to pinkish-tan colour typical of fresh Huon, plain straight grain, no birdseye. Top right corner has a large rough, crumbly patch along the edge (sapwood/cambium remnant, possibly some decay or borer) and the top end is split and ragged.
lots.condition: Rough sawn, unseasoned or air-dried status unknown, live edges, ragged top end and crumbly patch along one edge; usable area slightly reduced.
lots.question_for_gowans: What are the length, width and thickness of lot 1121, is it air-dried, and is the crumbly patch at the top edge soft rot or borer? Is the species confirmed as Huon pine?
lots.score_reason: Plain slab in a weekly commodity line; Gowans same-title hammers mostly $35 to $70.
